question: Will Argentina's Senate give media sanción to a bill suspending or eliminating the PASO primaries in its 26 November 2026 session?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no floor vote: government has an explicit December extraordinary-sessions fallback, so a short count leads to postponement. Independent counts as of Nov 15 put support at 31-32 of the 37 required; PRO (3) publicly skeptical and objecting to last-minute changes/colectoras; 3 UCR senators (Abad, Fama, Kroneberger) opposed; LLA bloc leader Bullrich says votes aren't there. For YES: committee dictamen reportedly secured for Nov 17, five UCR plus several governor-aligned senators committed, Feb 2025 precedent of successful Senate PASO suspension, and Peronist incentives to avoid primaries. Extra NO risk: reported presidential-only suspension variant would not count. No human market found (Polymarket blocked in Argentina; none on Manifold/Kalshi).
calls.dossier:
- Requirement: Art. 77 Constitution — 37 of 72 Senate votes (absolute majority of members) for electoral-regime change; LLA has 21, needs 16 more (multiple outlets, Nov 14-15 2026).
- Committee: Asuntos Constitucionales (19 members, 10 signatures for dictamen; LLA has 6) meets Tue 17 Nov 15:00, chaired by Agustín Coto; Noticias Argentinas (Nov 14) reports govt has committee majority; PRO's Goerling (Infobae Nov 15) doubts dictamen can pass if text keeps changing.
- Floor target: Thu 26 Nov, last ordinary session (ordinary period ends 30 Nov). Govt plan: Senate half-sanction in Nov, Deputies in December extraordinaries; govt has said it would use December extraordinaries for electoral reform if November fails.
- Counts: Infobae (Nov 15) estimates 31-32 votes; Total News Agency (Nov 15) says 31 of 37 secured; govt's most optimistic tally 38 (21 LLA + 10 UCR + 3 PRO + 4 provincial) per Infobae via reconquistaradios (Nov 14).
- Committed UCR: Vischi, Valenzuela (Corrientes), Schneider (Chaco), Galaretto, Losada (Santa Fe); possible: Suárez, Juri (Mendoza). Opposed UCR: Abad, Fama, Kroneberger (Noticias Argentinas Nov 14). Govt needs ~7 of 10 UCR.
- UCR condition: inclusion of 'colectoras'; allies also ask for Ficha Limpia. PRO (Goerling, Cristina, Huala) deciding Mon 16 Nov; Goerling: PASO 'should not be touched, especially so close to an election', calls colectoras 'absurd' (Infobae Nov 15).
- Governor-aligned senators from Catamarca, Neuquén, Córdoba, Chubut, Salta reportedly support (~5 votes). Peronism divided; CFK camp benefits from no primaries (Ámbito, Nov 15-16).
- Text scope: reports say suspension for 2027 only (not elimination); Infobae Nov 15 describes a version 'suspending PASO for presidential races' plus colectoras, higher party thresholds, financing changes — a presidential-only suspension would resolve NO; optional primaries also NO.
- Internal: Bullrich (LLA bloc chief) sidelined from negotiations, says votes aren't there; Santilli negotiating with governors (Mendoza mining summit Nov 19).
- Precedent: Feb 2025 Senate gave dictamen and approved the 2025 PASO suspension in extraordinary sessions.
- Markets: searched; Polymarket blocked in Argentina since March 2026, no PASO market found on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi.
- Resolution: resolves off a completed Senate approval (en general AND en particular) in the 26 Nov session (incl. continuation into 27 Nov), confirmed via credible reporting/senado.gob.ar; not off committee dictamen or Deputies.
- Event window: 26 Nov 2026 -> end of 27 Nov 2026 per criteria; as of 16 Nov 0% elapsed.
- Not found: formal convocatoria for 26 Nov session; final dictamen text; PRO's Monday decision.

PRO (3) publicly resists the new colectoras text and doubts dictamen; 3 UCR opposed; Bullrich says votes aren't there. December extraordinary sessions are an explicit fallback, making slippage the status quo. Upside: committee majority reportedly secured for 17 Nov, UCR-governor deals near closure, Feb 2025 precedent of a 43-20 Senate PASO suspension once governors aligned. calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) vote count, 36 per the government vs 30-32 in independent tallies. Search results only repeated the 'close to 37' framing plus the requirement of 7 of 10 UCR, all 3 PRO and 6 provincial votes; not settled, and both camps agree the government is short. (2) Text scope (presidential-only vs all offices): Parlamentario/APF 15 Nov describe the new text as suspending PASO 'only during 2027' with colectoras linked to presidential tickets, so the presidential wording seems to describe the colectoras, not a partial suspension; mostly settled toward full suspension. (3) PRO's Monday decision: not yet reported; PRO still resisting. (4) Formal convocatoria for 26 Nov: none found beyond the target date. Remaining weighting is judgment: slippage to December is the modal path, with real upside from governor deals. I land near the lower runs but slightly above them given the committee majority looks real.
